newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down, awaiting economic data.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down, awaiting economic data.

text.p: Thai stocks fell for the third consecutive trading day on Monday as investors stayed on the sidelines awaiting key economic indicators to be released by the central bank later this week, brokers said.
The SET index moved in the negative zone throughout the day and closed 6.79 points lower at 931.51 on thin 1.7 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index slipped 0.54 point to 70.22.
"Investors are waiting for economic indicators. They're also concerned about political stability ahead of the November election," said Somnuk Chanrasamee of Nava Finance and Securities.
Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa dissolved parliament last month and called a snap election for November 17.
Continued market talk that some property firms were having cashflow problems and were unable to settle debts with finance companies continued to be a negative factor in the market today, Somnuk said.

A senior executive of Juldis Develop, whose share price took a hit on the market talk last week, told Reuters on Monday that the company was not having cashflow trouble and most of the company's funds were raised through Euro convertible debentures.
All the major sectors on the board fell today.

Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 70.50. Juldis Develop was unchanged at 36 while TelecomAsia rose 0.50 to 51.50 and Finance One, Thailand's largest finance company, slipped one to 65.
Brokers said the SET index is expected to retreat a bit further on Tuesday as the market lacks positive news to boost investment.
Support is seen at around 920 points on Tuesday while resistance is pegged around 950, brokers said.
